harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Created the appworker account on node1 and configured its login sessions to a hard/soft limit of 8192 open files and 256 processes via /etc/security/limits.d/appworker.conf. Verified live via a real PAM login session (su -) both before and after a full node restart, which was confirmed by a changed boot_id.
actions_performed: Inspected OS (Ubuntu 16.04 Xenial) and confirmed appworker did not already exist
Wrote /etc/security/limits.d/appworker.conf with soft/hard nofile 8192 and soft/hard nproc 256
Investigated PAM config (common-session lacks pam_limits.so; login and su include it directly) and verified limits apply correctly via `su - appworker`
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id, account existence, limits file contents, live ulimit values
Issued a backgrounded `shutdown -r now` on node1 so the acknowledgement returned before disconnection
Polled node1 until exec access returned
Confirmed boot_id changed, proving an actual restart occurred
Re-verified appworker account, limits file, and live ulimit values post-restart

evidence.summary: useradd succeeded and getent passwd shows appworker:x:1001:1001::/home/appworker:/bin/bash

evidence.requirement: Login sessions limited to 8192 open files and 256 processes
evidence.summary: limits.d/appworker.conf sets soft/hard nofile 8192 and soft/hard nproc 256; live `su - appworker` login session shows ulimit -n=8192 and ulimit -u=256 (sudo -i path was shown not to apply limits due to missing pam_limits in common-session-noninteractive, so su/login path was used and confirmed)
Captured boot_id b185f188-42be-40d1-84ea-f7c9a76f5c8d plus account and limits verification prior to reboot
Node briefly refused connections (cmd-9e4502c25add47c8), then came back with boot_id b57adfa5-f520-46ee-894d-25d59f4472f3, different from the pre-restart b185f188...

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of account and limits
evidence.summary: After restart, appworker account, limits.d config file, and live su - appworker ulimit values (8192 files / 256 processes) all match pre-restart state
